# xDBML -- compact reference for AI assistants

> xDBML is a text markup language to describe the semantics of structured and semi-structured data across relational, document, columnar, graph, view, and exchange formats. xDBML extends DBML into a true metadata and semantic data modeling language with richer support for validation, semantics, cardinality, annotations, and AI-friendly metadata, while deliberately staying readable and Git-friendly. When a user asks you to design, draft, edit, or render a schema for use with an xDBML tool, write xDBML -- not plain DBML -- and reach for the xDBML constructs below where they fit. Plain DBML still parses (it is a subset), but it misses the structures and metadata that make xDBML worth using.

## How to author

- Start every document with a version line: `xdbml: 0.5`
- Use `Entity` for a generic entity. Target-native synonyms also work and carry intent: `Table` (relational), `Collection` (document/MongoDB), `Record` (Avro). Namespacing uses `Container`, `Database`, `Schema`, `Bucket`, `Keyspace`, or `Namespace`.
- Prefer xDBML extensions over flat DBML: nested objects and arrays, polymorphism (`oneOf` / `union`), reusable `Type`s, precise min/max cardinality, `Edge`s, `View`s, supertype groups for generalization, and AI-readiness metadata (`synonyms`, `business_term`, `tags`, `granularity`).
- A field line is `name  type  [settings]`. Settings are comma-separated inside `[ ]`.

## Core constructs

Version, project, reusable type:

```
xdbml: 0.5

Project shop {
  targets: [PostgreSQL, MongoDB]
  Note: 'Single source of truth.'
}

Type Address {
  street  varchar [not null]
  city    varchar
  country varchar [default: 'US']
}
```

Entity and fields (relational):

```
Entity customers {
  Note: 'One row per registered customer'
  id      int     [pk]
  email   varchar [unique, not null, pattern: '^[^@]+@[^@]+$', tags: ['pii']]
  address Address
}
```

Common field settings: `pk`, `unique`, `not null`, `default: <v>`, `note: '...'`, `pattern: '...'`, `minimum: N`, `maximum: N`, `maxLength: N`, `tags: [...]`, `synonyms: [...]`, `business_term: '...'`, `granularity: <unit>`.

Relationships (foreign keys), inline or as a block:

```
copy_id int [ref: > copies.id, not null]

Ref: orders.customer_id > customers.id [source: '1..*', target: '1..1']
```

Operators: `>` many-to-one, `<` one-to-many, `-` one-to-one, `<>` many-to-many. The optional `[source: '<min>..<max>', target: '<min>..<max>']` is xDBML's precise cardinality.

A relationship can record denormalization rather than a key reference. Add `foreign_master` when the child attribute holds a copy of the parent's value, as document models often do; nothing is generated from it, it takes one attribute on each side, and a child attribute has at most one master:

```
customerName string [ref: > customers.name, foreign_master]

Ref: orders.shipTo.city > customers.address.city [foreign_master]
```

Relationships carry documentation for conceptual and logical modeling. Roles name what each end plays, verbs read the relationship in each direction, and `constraint_type` records whether the child's foreign key is part of its primary key. None of it reaches a generator:

```
Ref places: orders.customerID > customers.customerID [
  source_role: 'shopping cart', source_verb: 'is bought by',
  target_role: 'buyer',         target_verb: 'places',
  constraint_type: non_identifying
]
```

An endpoint may also name an entity and stop there, for a relationship drawn before either entity has attributes. Such a relationship states no cardinality until one is written, takes its reading direction from the operator alone (`-` meaning linked with no direction stated), and accepts `undirected: true` for one that reads the same way both ways:

```
Entity Customer { }
Entity Order { }

Ref: Customer > Order [target_verb: 'places']
```

Generalization (supertype and subtypes) is a `SupertypeGroup`: one supertype, its subtypes along one axis, and whether every supertype instance is one of them (`completeness: total | partial`) and whether it can be several (`exclusivity: disjoint | overlapping`); leave either out when it is not known. Each subtype declares only its own attributes; never repeat the supertype's, that is an error. Use one group per axis: a supertype may anchor several groups, an entity is a subtype in one group only, and a subtype may be the supertype of another group. The group name is required and names the axis:

```
Entity Party {
  party_id int [pk]
  name     varchar
}
Entity Person {
  birth_date date
}
Entity Organization {
  legal_form varchar
}

SupertypeGroup legal_nature [supertype: Party, completeness: total, exclusivity: disjoint, strategy: roll_up, merge: flat, discriminator: nature] {
  Person
  Organization [strategy: roll_down]
}
```

`strategy` (`preserved_hierarchy`, `roll_up`, `roll_down`, also per subtype), `merge` (`flat`, `nested`) and `discriminator` record how a physical model is meant to be derived; they add nothing to the logical model, and `discriminator` is not allowed on an overlapping group. To point a relationship at a subtype, name the subtype as an entity: `Ref: assignments.employee_id > Employee`, not `Employee.party_id`.

Nesting (documents, structs, arrays):

```
Entity orders {
  _id        objectId [pk]
  line_items array [
    line_item object {
      sku   string     [not null]
      qty   int32      [minimum: 1]
      price Decimal128
    }
  ]
}
```

Polymorphism:

```
payment oneOf {
  card object { last4 string }
  bank object { iban string }
} [discriminator: kind]

score union [int, decimal, null]
```

Graph edge (a relationship with its own properties -- use this, not a `Ref`, when the relationship itself carries attributes):

```
Edge KNOWS [source: Person, target: Person, source_cardinality: '0..*', target_cardinality: '0..*'] {
  since date [not null]
}
```

View:

```
View top_customers [materialized: true] {
  source_query: '''SELECT id, SUM(total) AS ltv FROM orders GROUP BY id'''
  id  int [pk]
  ltv decimal(15,2)
}
```

AI-readiness and custom metadata:

```
mrr decimal [synonyms: ['monthly revenue'], business_term: 'MRR', tags: ['kpi'], granularity: month]

Entity customers [x_owner: 'data-team@acme.com', x_retention_days: 2555] { id int [pk] }
```

Types: relational (`int`, `bigint`, `varchar`, `decimal(p,s)`, `boolean`, `date`, `timestamp`, ...) and BSON/Avro-native (`objectId`, `int32`, `int64`, `Decimal128`, `string`, `Date`, `BinData`, ...) are all recognized and preserved through round-trips.

## Minimal complete example

```
xdbml: 0.5

Entity members {
  id        int     [pk]
  email     varchar [unique, not null, tags: ['pii']]
  joined_at timestamp
}

Entity books {
  id    int     [pk]
  isbn  varchar [unique, not null]
  title varchar [not null]
}

Entity copies {
  id      int     [pk]
  book_id int     [ref: > books.id, not null]
  barcode varchar [unique, not null]
}

Entity loans {
  id          int       [pk]
  copy_id     int       [ref: > copies.id, not null]
  member_id   int       [ref: > members.id, not null]
  loaned_at   timestamp [not null]
  due_at      timestamp [not null]
  returned_at timestamp
}
```
